uncited: Voxel Face Packing is a bitstream encoding method that compresses voxel spatial coordinates, material identity, and face orientation into a single 32-bit integer.

It solves the problem of high vertex buffer overhead and frequent state changes in large voxel grid rendering by allowing all necessary geometry data to be packed into a compact, cache-friendly format.
The values are packed into a single 32-bit integer using bitwise shifts and logical OR operations.
Values are recovered by shifting right and masking with bitwise AND.
Ensure inputs are integers before packing.
Overflow or underflow will corrupt the bit layout.
Their values in the packed integer are undefined and should be ignored during unpacking.
- **Time Complexity:** Packing and unpacking are $O(1)$ operations involving a constant number of bitwise shifts and logical operations.
- **Memory Complexity:** Reduces memory footprint per vertex from multiple variables (e.g., 4 floats or ints) to a single 32-bit integer.
Not suitable for high-precision coordinates or large numbers of material types without extension.
This method is described in the context of web-based voxel terrain rendering, specifically in the `web_voxel_terrain` project.
It is designed to optimize rendering performance by minimizing the data transferred to the GPU and simplifying vertex shader logic.
